title: paged-kv-cache: block allocator reuse + locality-aware pinning + TTL cleanup
author: Alex Chen
description:
Motivation: The paged KV cache has shown alloc churn and suboptimal locality in multi-tenant steady-state workloads, increasing tail latency and memory pressure. This PR introduces three related improvements: 1) allocator reuse for block allocations to avoid repeated mmap/free churn across requests, 2) locality-aware pinning so hot keys/blocks are pinned to the same GPU-local allocator region to improve cache-line locality and reduce cross-device traffic, and 3) TTL-based background cleanup for expired pinned ranges to bound memory usage.

Changes in this PR: checklist:
- [x] Rework BlockAllocator to support a reuse pool and per-thread arenas (src/runtime/kv_cache/block_allocator.rs)
- [x] Add locality-aware pinning API and heuristics in BlockManager (src/runtime/kv_cache/block_manager.rs)
- [x] Implement TTL eviction sweeper with low-priority background task (src/runtime/kv_cache/ttl_sweeper.rs)
- [x] Add unit and integration tests for reuse/pinning/ttl (tests/kv_cache/*)
- [x] Add microbench harness and perf dashboard queries (bench/kv_cache_reuse_bench.toml, docs/perf/kv_cache.md)
- [x] Update runtime scheduler batching policy to prefer pinned-local allocations when possible (src/runtime/scheduler/batching.rs)

High-level summary of behavior changes: allocator reuse dramatically reduces the number of system allocations and fragmentation under high churn workloads (many short-lived contexts). The locality-aware pinning tries to keep frequently-used blocks pinned to the same NUMA/GPU-local region; this reduces cross-device copies for KV cache fill and reduces pressure on the interconnect. TTL sweeper prevents pinned ranges from leaking indefinitely in long-running workloads. All changes are backwards-compatible configuration toggles and off by default for private deployments.

Implementation notes: the BlockAllocator now exposes a small fixed-size reuse pool keyed by block size class and device region; allocations first consult the per-thread arena then the reuse pool before hitting the system allocator. Pinning metadata now includes a locality tag (region id) and a pin score that decays over time; BlockManager uses an eviction policy that prefers unpinning blocks with low pin score and remote locality. The TTL sweeper runs at a configurable interval and respects a budgeted work quantum to avoid interference with inference.

Benchmarks & results (representative):
- Long-context chat workload (seq=4096, mixed tenant): p99 latency reduced 8.3% at 95th percentile load; p50 unchanged
- Throughput (tokens/sec) improved 18% under simulated reuse-heavy traffic (steady reusing of prefixes)
- Memory fragmentation/overhead decreased ~42% in our synthetic churn benchmark (alloc/free heavy)
- KV cache hit-rate improved 6-12% for workloads with hot prefixes due to locality pinning

Rollout plan: feature guarded behind runtime flags. Staged rollout on Dedicated first (+canary fleet), collect p99 latency, cross-device bandwidth, and memory metrics. Disable by default for Private until validated on on-prem infra (TTL default=24h, reuse pool size conservative).

Backward compatibility / migration: No wire-protocol changes. Operators can tune reuse_pool_size, pinning_enabled, and ttl_seconds via node config.

References: ENG-2248 (allocator churn), ENG-2281 (pinning strategy), internal perf dashboards (link omitted).
